picks.excerpt: Three Epic Games veterans — including former Unreal lead evangelist Sjoerd De Jong and ex-Unreal product director Arjan Brussee — detail Immens, a European game engine whose architecture, tooling and asset pipelines are built from scratch around AI agents rather than bolting AI on. They pitch it as a way for small teams to cut cost and dev time amid mounting discontent with Unity and Unreal.
picks.rationale: A new engine designed around AI agents from the architecture up is the most consequential tooling story in the pool — it changes what a small team's pipeline could look like.

picks.excerpt: Wolf Haus's co-founders explain how a 12-person team is shipping the large-scale cult simulator Join Us using in-house tech and explicitly no generative AI — a counter-case to the 'AI lets small teams do AAA' pitch, arguing custom tooling and Hollywood-style production discipline do the same job.
picks.rationale: The direct counter-case to pick 1: custom tooling and production discipline, not genAI, as the way a 12-person team reaches large-scale scope.

picks.excerpt: Players in China spotted a free-trial watermark for ByteDance's Doubao AI image tool left on in-game seahorse artwork in Neverness To Everness' 1.3 update — an accidental disclosure of generative AI in a shipped live-service art pipeline.
picks.rationale: A shipped live-service update leaked its own AI tool watermark — the plainest possible reminder that asset QA now has to check for provenance artifacts.

picks.excerpt: A long feature on generative AI inside the Skyrim modding scene, reported from the perspective of players, modders and the mod-hosting sites themselves — including why disclosure tagging keeps failing and how UGC platforms are struggling to build workable AI policy.
picks.rationale: Reported from inside a UGC platform, it shows exactly where AI disclosure tagging breaks down — the practical problem every community-facing product now has.

picks.excerpt: CD Projekt Red couldn't ship the NPC fear-reaction system it prototyped for The Witcher 3 because emergent crowd behaviour broke in horrifying ways — a concrete case study in how hard believable autonomous NPC behaviour actually is to tune.
picks.rationale: A concrete failure case for autonomous NPC behaviour, useful ballast for anyone now wiring LLM-driven NPCs into an open world.
